    Remove Diacritics and Transliterate Ligatures

    remove_diacritics.Rd

    Strips diacritical marks (accents, umlauts, cedillas, tildes, etc.) and transliterates common Latin ligatures/special characters (e.g., œ -> oe, æ -> ae, ß -> ss, ø -> o) into their base ASCII equivalents.

    Usage

    remove_diacritics(x)

    Arguments

    x

    A character vector from which diacritics should be stripped.

    Value

    A character vector of the same length as x with diacritics removed and ligatures expanded.

    Details

    The function uses an internal precomputed lookup table derived from the Unicode Character Database (UCD) canonical decomposition rules and extended Latin mappings.

    Performance is optimized by checking whether any character in the input string requires replacement before performing string reconstruction. If a string contains only ASCII characters or characters without diacritics, it is returned immediately without memory reallocation.

    Missing values (NA) and empty strings ("") are preserved as-is.

    See also

    to_lower_unicode()

    Examples

    # Common French/Spanish accents
remove_diacritics(c("Café", "Crème brûlée", "El Niño", "Façade"))
#> [1] "Cafe"         "Creme brulee" "El Nino"      "Facade"      

# Ligatures and special Latin characters
remove_diacritics(c("Cœur", "Encyclopædia", "Fußball", "København"))
#> [1] "Coeur"         "Encyclopaedia" "Fussball"      "København"    

# Combined with case transformation
raw_text <- c("HÉLÈNE", "À bientôt !")
remove_diacritics(to_lower_unicode(raw_text))
#> [1] "helene"      "a bientot !"

# Edge cases: empty strings and missing values
remove_diacritics(c("Simple ASCII", "", NA_character_))
#> [1] "Simple ASCII" ""             NA
